result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is the better quiz. Every item is a realistic floor situation, and its key explains why each option is right or wrong. B adds a few details that aren't in the session, like a substitute truck, a rated truck and the reason a load slides off, and a few distractors such as 'speed up' are weak. It also leaves out fork height and mast tilt. A sticks closely to the session list and covers more topics, but almost every question asks the hire to recite a rule or number, and its key only restates the rule without addressing the tempting wrong answer. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer A builds each question around a real situation on the floor, and its key explains why every option is right or wrong, so it does much better on rubric items 1, 4 and 3. Its weak spots are small: it skips fork travel height and mast tilt, and it adds a few minor ideas like 'take a different truck' and 'loads slide off'. Answer B covers more of the session, but most of its questions ask people to recite a rule or number, and its key only repeats the rule without saying why the tempting wrong options fail.
